items.title: Schema: optional one-word keyword on a catalog item
items.action: Add `keyword` to `$defs/item.properties` of TodoCatalog.schema.json, right after `title`: type string, pattern and maxLength per values V1/V2, description naming it the one word that jogs a reader's memory of the item on the working-refs line. Not in `required`; absent means no keyword (null is refused, so a catalog never carries a null key a pinned schema would reject).

items.title: keywords.py: the high-confidence guesser and the catalog fill
items.action: New module harness_lib/todo_sync/keywords.py. `guess_keyword(item)` reads `title` and `files`: (1) a title prefix `<word>: ` whose word matches V1 and is not a generic prefix (V4) wins; (2) else the file stems (name up to the first dot, a leading `test_` dropped, generic stems V3 and stems starting with `_` skipped): exactly one distinct stem, or one stem counted at least twice and more often than any other, wins; (3) else None. A guess failing V1/V2 is None. `fill_keywords(catalog)` returns a dataclass (`catalog`, `set`, `left`) on a deep copy: every item without a keyword gets the guess inserted right after `title`; an item with one keeps it; no guess leaves the key absent. `apply_keywords(cfg, dry_run=False)` loads the catalog with `load_catalog(cfg, 'keywords')` and writes it through `write_edits(cfg, dump_like(...))` as `reshape._apply` does. `keyword_lines(fill, dry_run)` prints `keywords: set N, left M without one` (`would set` on a dry run) then one `set <id>: <keyword>` line each. `require_keywords(specs)` raises TodoSyncError `item <n> lacks keyword (suggested: <guess>)` or `item <n> lacks keyword (no confident guess: name the module, skill or class it is about)` for a spec item whose keyword is absent or blank.

anchors.expect: raw, data = load_catalog(cfg, verb) out = fn(data) if not dry_run and out.catalog != data: write_edits(cfg, dump_like(out.catalog, raw))

items.title: inbox put requires a keyword; add and the drain keep it
items.action: reshape.py: `keyword` joins ADD_OPTIONAL (so UPDATE_FIELDS takes it, updates.py:21), _TYPE_RULES checks it as a non-empty string, and _item_fields places it right after `title` when the spec sets it. inbox.put calls keywords.require_keywords(specs) right after read_spec, before _validate (D2 inbox-put): an `add --spec` run and the drain stay optional. put_updates is unchanged. The put spec builders `_item` in test_todo_sync_inbox.py and test_todo_sync_catalog_lock_cli.py gain a keyword (sweep S1).

items.title: todo_sync.py suggest-keyword and keywords subcommands
items.action: `suggest-keyword --spec PATH` (unlocked, reads the `items` list through read_spec) prints `item <n>: <guess>` or `item <n>: none` per item (D3). `keywords [--dry-run] [--lease TOKEN]` joins GUARDED and _write: it runs keywords.apply_keywords and prints keyword_lines. Both get a section in todo_sync.md (test_todo_sync_usage_doc requires one per command and every option named), and the `inbox put` section there names the keyword refusal.

items.title: working-refs: label each TODO id with its keyword
items.action: mirror.ts exports KEYWORD_KEY = 'keyword'. hide.ts adds `keywordsOf(text)`: the catalog's item id -> keyword map, items without a string keyword skipped, empty for an absent or malformed catalog. watch.ts readHide parses the catalog text once for both retired ids and keywords; HideState and LineView (line.ts) carry `keywords`. formatRefs takes the map and labels each id per D1 (an id without a keyword prints alone); buildLine uses it for the own refs and every other-branch segment, and the cap counts the labelled text. statusText draws the same labels: WorkingLine (types/index.d.ts) gains `refs`, the formatted own-refs text, so statusText stops re-formatting the ids. The line.ts doc comment drops the claim that formatRefs matches harness_lib.working_refs.format_refs (the Python reply stays unlabelled). Tests in hide/line/watch .test.ts; README examples show a labelled id. Colors (D1 space-color): on the ccstatusline form only, each `todo-xxxx keyword` label (the id alone when it has no keyword) is wrapped in `[38;5;<n>m` ... RESET_FG, n picked per V5/V6 by an exported `todoColor(id)`, in the own refs and in every other-branch segment; issues, plan links and the plain form stay uncolored, and the cap still measures the plain text. The structured refs the colored form needs ride on WorkingLine and OtherSegment instead of re-parsing text.

values.value: ANSI 256 colors 39, 170, 36, 214, 141, 72, 203, 178; never 240 (DARK, other branch names)

values.value: FNV-1a 32-bit of the canonical id, modulo the palette length, so a TODO keeps its color across sessions, branches and segments
